title: What Is Twin-Lens Reflex (Rolleiflex)? — Definition
body:
Photography is fixing light's image permanently: from the camera obscura through daguerreotypes, wet plates, dry plates, roll film, 35mm, Polaroid instant, and color processes like Kodachrome — the chemical century of image-making before digital sensors.

In the context of this database, the Twin-Lens Reflex (Rolleiflex) is presented as one photography record among the photography history family. The 1929 Rolleiflex: waist-level 6x6 — the portrait/wedding camera.

title: Origins and History of Twin-Lens Reflex (Rolleiflex)
body:
The Twin-Lens Reflex (Rolleiflex) belongs to the 1929–1970s era and traces to Franke & Heidecke.

Niépce fixed the first permanent image (~1826, 8-hour exposure); Daguerre's daguerreotype (1839) made portraits practical. Wet collodion (1851) sharpened detail; dry plates (1870s) freed photographers from portable darkrooms. Eastman's roll film (1888) and the $1 Brownie (1900) put cameras in every home — 'You press the button, we do the rest.' 35mm (Leica, 1925) made photography nimble; Kodachrome (1935) made it color. Polaroid's instant film (1948/1972 SX-70) made it immediate. Japanese SLRs (Nikon F, 1959; Pentax, Canon) democratized quality; the 1990s APS was film's last new format before digital swept all away.

Within that longer story, Twin-Lens Reflex (Rolleiflex): The viewing lens; the 2.8F's perfection. The Rollei is the TLR's icon.

title: How Twin-Lens Reflex (Rolleiflex) Works
body:
Light through a lens exposes silver-halide crystals in emulsion; developer reduces exposed crystals to metallic silver (the negative); fixer removes unexposed halide; printing reverses the tones onto paper. Color film stacks three emulsion layers sensitive to blue, green, red, with dye couplers forming cyan, magenta, yellow dyes (subtractive). Instant film (Polaroid) pods spread reagent across the exposed sheet, developing and fixing in one sealed sandwich. Exposure balances aperture, shutter speed, and film speed (ISO/ASA) — the exposure triangle.

Applied to the Twin-Lens Reflex (Rolleiflex) (1929–1970s, Franke & Heidecke): The Rollei is the TLR's icon.

The engineering principles above are exactly what made this class of technology practical: every unit is a working compromise between materials, energy, precision, and cost.

title: Photography History Glossary
body:
The working vocabulary of photography history:

• daguerreotype — Silvered copper plate; mirror-like one-of-a-kind image (1839).
• tintype / ambrotype — Cheap iron-plate and glass variants for the masses.
• wet collodion — Sticky-plate process; tack-sharp, darkroom on the spot.
• dry plate — Gelatin emulsion; the first convenient negative.
• Brownie — Kodak's $1 box camera (1900); snapshot culture begins.
• 35mm / 135 — Leica's cine-film format; the century's standard.
• 120 / 620 / 127 — Roll-film formats for medium format and hobbyists.
• Kodachrome — 1935 color slide film; legendary saturation and archive life.
• C-41 / E-6 — Color negative and slide processing standards.
• D-76 — Kodak's classic B&W developer; the reference soup.
• push / pull — Over/under-developing to shift effective film speed.
• sunny 16 — f/16 at 1/ISO on a sunny day; the meter-free rule.

title: Twin-Lens Reflex (Rolleiflex) Restoration Guide
body:
Cameras: clean, don't force; lighter fluid frees stuck helicoids (carefully). Replace light seals (foam kits). Shutters: exercise, then CLA (clean-lube-adjust). Lenses: fungus needs disassembly; haze sometimes cleans. Never open a camera with film inside in light.

Restoration order for a Twin-Lens Reflex (Rolleiflex): 1) document everything photographically before touching it; 2) stabilize (clean, de-corrode, free seized parts); 3) repair before replacing; 4) replace only what is missing or dangerous, marking replacements; 5) test under supervision. Never power an unrestored electrical photography record without a current-limited bring-up.

title: Twin-Lens Reflex (Rolleiflex) — Sunny-16 exposure calculator (Runnable Python)
body:
Computes shutter/aperture pairs from the sunny-16 rule and depth-of-field basics — the meter-free math photographers carried in their heads.

The program below is real, runnable Python 3. Save it as demo.py and run `python3 demo.py`. It models the core mathematics of the Twin-Lens Reflex (Rolleiflex) so you can experiment with the parameters yourself.
code:
# Sunny-16 + exposure triangle (public-domain photographic math)
def sunny16(iso):
    # bright sun: f/16, shutter = 1/ISO
    return 16, f"1/{iso}"

CONDITIONS = {"bright sun": 0, "hazy sun": 1, "cloudy bright": 2,
              "overcast": 3, "sunset/open shade": 4}
def exposure(iso, condition):
    stops = CONDITIONS[condition]
    # open up `stops` from f/16 at 1/ISO
    apertures = [16, 11, 8, 5.6, 4, 2.8, 2]
    ap = apertures[min(stops, len(apertures)-1)]
    return ap, f"1/{iso}"

for cond in CONDITIONS:
    ap, sh = exposure(400, cond)
    print(f"ISO 400, {cond:16s} -> f/{ap} at {sh}s")

# Depth of field hyperfocal (simplified): H = f^2 / (N * c)
def hyperfocal(f_mm, n, coc_mm=0.03):
    return f_mm**2 / (n * coc_mm) / 1000
print(f"\n50mm f/8 hyperfocal: {hyperfocal(50, 8):.1f} m (focus here, everything sharp)")
